newsitem.title: USA: U.S. weekly cash lumber review - March 7.
newsitem.headline: U.S. weekly cash lumber review - March 7.

text.p: Random Lengths Gross List Cash Lumber Prices Quotes:
(2x4 Std&Btr) WEEKLY MIDWEEK PREV WK YR AGO

COMMENT - The market's wobbly course over the last two weeks came to an end as price tilted to the downside, led by Canadian items, Random Lengths said in its weekly review. Buyers appeared convinced that there would be no shortage of lumber as the quota year expires on March 31, the lumber reporting agency said.

Some traders feared a last-minute push of Canadian lumber into the U.S. this month, Random Lengths said. Canadian fee-free quota exports as of Feb 27 were running at 69.4 percent of the quarterly Jan-Mar quota and 94.4 pct of annual April/Mar quota.

Wholesalers turned bearish during the week, citing seasonal price trends, historically high prices, and forecasts that output will taper off during the year. Prices moved in both directions but the downside moves were more numerous.
Weather continued to play a major role, slowing demand but also hampering production in the South Central region. Dealers digested earlier purchases, picking off best offers from mills.
Secondaries also tried to reduce their bought-ahead positions by offering more wood, Random Lengths said. Treaters maintained a low profile, buying mostly on a replacement basis.

Reports of inventories in the field varied, but some buyers reported adequate-to-heavy stocks at reloads. Mills countered that a large volume of wood has been backed up by weather and will quickly move when job sites dry out, the agency said.

Wholesalers tried to stir up business with short sales or hefty counters to mill quotes, but producers often turned away from the deeper cuts. Some traders planning to attend next week's WWPA meeting decided to wait and assess the tone there.
Some sellers talked up Tuesday's bullish report on January new home sales, in particular the low backlog of unsold units.
Cedar prices leveled off, sparking a debate over whether the market was taking a needed pause or whether high prices were pushing buyers to alternative products, Random Lengths said.
